plan.english: Let him go below, into the darkness.

notes: The Lower Darkness as the destination of the dead (West 2007 ch. 10): Ved. ádharaṃ ... támaḥ, Lat. infernae tenebrae (Aen. 7.325, cited by West; the Lucretius and Catullus loci are from the local corpus). támas : tenebrae (*témH-s-) and ádhara- : inferus/infernus (*n̥dʰero-) are cognate; the lexicon has the adverb *Hn̥dʰér 'below' but no usable adjective, so 'lower' is rendered as an adverb (root-level match). Ved. gamaya is a causative ('make him go'); a plain 3sg imperative of *gʷem- is used and is Vedic-only, interpolated.

plan.english: The Twin's two dogs guard the path.

notes: The dog(s) guarding the way to the dead (West 2007 ch. 10 'Beware of the Dog'): Yama's two dogs (dual śvā́nau, 'path-guarding'), the two dogs of Vd. 13.9 (dual spāna) that guard the bridge, and the hound of Hades (Kerberos). Only *ḱwṓ is shared across branches. 'The Twin' (yemHós = Yama) is Vedic in this passage; Av. -pāna 'guarding' continues *peh₂- but is Indo-Iranian only; 'path' (Ved. pathi-) likewise. The dual follows Vedic and Avestan. The four-eyed (caturakṣá-, Av. caϑru.cašma-) and spotted (śabála-, perhaps = Κέρβερος) epithets have no usable lexeme.

plan.english: You put them down to sleep.

notes: Killing as 'putting to sleep' with the causative *swop-éye-: Ved. (ní) svāpaya- of Indra's foes (West 2007 ch. 10 lists RV 1.121.11, 4.30.21, 7.19.4, 9.97.54), OE swebban 'put to sleep, kill' (Beowulf 680 in the local Harrison–Sharp text; āswefede 'put to sleep by swords' 567), Lat. sōpīre (Lucr. 3.904 leto sopitus 'put to sleep by death'). Past (imperfect) as in Ved. ásvāpayaḥ, 2sg addressed to the god. ní 'down' and the pronoun object are Vedic-only, interpolated.

The slain one lies (Watkins 1995, 'slain-lies' and 'slay-lie-sleep' formulas): *ḱey- in Ved. śayadhve, Av. sōire, Gk κεῖμαι; the participle *gʷʰn̥tós in Ved. hatá-, Av. jata-, Gk πρό-σ-φατος 'freshly slain' (Il. 24.757). Opening 'now' follows Gk νῦν and OE nū (OE ligeð is from *legʰ-, a different root). 3sg follows Il. 18.20 (Vedic 2pl, Avestan 3pl, Il. 24.757 2sg).

Lying and sleep in one passage for the slain: Vṛtra 'lying' (ā-śáyāna-, *ḱey-) is put to sleep (siṣvapaḥ) by Indra's weapon; the slain Iphidamas 'lay down in the bronze sleep' (κοιμήσατο, a *ḱey- derivative, with ὕπνον = *supnós); the dead dragon 'lies, sleeps' (Beowulf). *supnós is the Greek ablaut form; Ved. svap- and OE swefan are root-level matches. Locative 'in sleep' is interpolated (Greek has a cognate accusative).

Watkins 1995 (nectar as *neḱ-tr̥h₂- 'overcoming death'): Ved. áti tarāṇi mṛtyúm 'may I cross beyond death' (subjunctive 1sg). Only *terh₂- is shared; the death noun is renewed (Ved. mṛtyú-, Gk νεκ-), so *mértis (Ved. mṛtí-, Lat. mors) is interpolated, as is *éti 'over' (= Ved. áti).

plan.english: Having crossed death, he has reached what is immortal.

notes: Watkins 1995: Īśā Up. 14 'having crossed death ... he attains the immortal' encodes both halves of Gk νέκταρ τε καὶ ἀμβροσίην: *neḱ-terh₂- 'overcoming death' and *n̥-mr̥-to- 'undying' (Ved. amṛ́tam, Gk ἀμβροσίη). *h₂neḱ- 'reach' (Ved. aśnute, present) is Vedic only and interpolated; the perfect 'has reached' renders the attained state. Death noun interpolated as in death-otherworld-006.

Crossing to the dead (West 2007 ch. 10): the Chinvat 'crossing' (pərətu- = *pértus, cf. Lat. portus) of the Gāthās and Vīdēvdād; Patroclus' shade begs burial 'that I may pass the gates of Hades' (περήσω). Root-level: Avestan has the noun, Greek the verb of *per- 'cross'. 1sg prospective follows the Greek future; Y. 46.10 is likewise Zarathustra's first-person promise. The figura (verb + cognate noun) is the projection's; neither passage has both words.

Dying as going to (join) the dead (West 2007 ch. 10): Hector 'thought to reach the dead and the house of Hades this day'; OIr techt do écaib 'going to the dead' (idiom, quoted from West). Gk νέκυς and OIr éc (< *n̥ḱu-) continue *néḱus. The verbs are not cognate (ἱκνέομαι, techt); *gʷem- 'come' is interpolated.

Watkins 1995 'bring death': Gk φόνον φέρειν, ON banorð bera 'bear (someone's) death-word, cause his death'. φόνος is *gʷʰónos; ON bana- (bani 'slayer, death') is an n-stem of the same o-grade, a root-level match. Plural as in Il. 2.352; the dative of the victims is left out.

plan.english: The Twin died first of mortals.

notes: Yama, 'who died first of mortals' (AV 18.3.13) and chose death (RV 10.13.4); his Iranian counterpart Yima (Y. 9.4–5, where under his rule there was no death — the Avestan passage denies death in his reign, his fall follows in Yt. 19); ON Ymir is the cosmogonic Twin (West 2007 chs. 9–10). Only the name *yemHós 'twin' is shared beyond Indo-Iranian. The death verb and 'mortals' are Indo-Iranian only (Ved. mamā́ra, mártya-; Av. mərəϑiiu-, maṣ̌iia-) and interpolated; 'first' renders Ved. prathamá- with the lexicon's *pr̥h₂wós.
